title: Time-varying neural network for stock return prediction

extraction.methodology_summary: The authors propose an online early stopping (OES) algorithm for training neural networks in a time-varying context by treating the number of optimization iterations as a learnable, time-varying parameter updated recursively over time. The strategy is tested on predicting cross-sectional U.S. stock returns using firm-level features and industry dummy variables. Performance is evaluated out-of-sample using information coefficients, decile portfolio spreads, and Sharpe ratios compared against expanding window deep neural network (DNN) benchmarks.
extraction.universe: U.S. stocks listed on NYSE, AMEX, and NASDAQ (with an alternative investable universe excluding microcaps based on the 5th percentile of NYSE market capitalization breakpoints)

By contrast, mean decile spread and Sharpe ratio remain stable for OES, at 2.41 % and 0.82, respectively.

However, DNN experienced a significant drop in mean decile spread (to 1.69 % per month) and Sharpe ratio (0.69), suggesting that microcaps are significant contributors to the results using the full data set.

key_findings: The proposed online early stopping (OES) algorithm allows a neural network to adapt to time-varying asset pricing relationships without assuming explicit functional forms for concept drift.
OES outperforms static expanding window deep neural networks in predicting cross-sectional U.S. stock returns as measured by information coefficient (IC).
Firm-level feature importance exhibits rapid drops during periods of market distress (such as the 1990-91 recession, Dot-com bubble, and GFC), while industry indicators increase in importance.
Excluding microcap stocks improves predictive performance metrics (IC and R2) and shows that OES performance is robust and not driven solely by illiquid microcaps.
An ensemble of OES and standard DNN predictions lowers variance and achieves superior IC, decile spreads, and Sharpe ratios.
limitations: The algorithm has an inability to theoretically explain the underlying sources of variability in the changing function.
OES predictions exhibit higher variance, potentially requiring higher or different forms of regularization.
